data.cultural_impact: The name "Citra" is believed to have originated from the Sanskrit word for citrus fruit. In Islamic culture, citrus fruits have played an essential role in various aspects of daily life. For instance, they were commonly used to ward off evil, as the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) had said that citrus fruits were a source of blessings. Additionally, during weddings and festivities in Middle Eastern countries, citrus fruits, such as oranges, are thrown at the bride and groom, symbolizing greetings of joy and longevity. Moreover, citrus fruits were traditionally placed in mosques, and some believe that the fragrance of citrus fruits in a mosque can bring a deeper sense of concentration and focus during prayers.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Citra" carries deeper symbolism. "Citra" means "image" or "manifestation" in Sanskrit. In Islamic tradition, Allah (GOD) creates the image or manifestation of His infinite mercy and kindness through His creation, including the citrus fruits. The Quran describes Allah's mercy as "generous" (Ar-Rahman) and "compassionate" (Ar-Rahim). This compassion manifests in various forms, and citrus fruits are just one of them. The Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) also emphasized the significance of good character and kind intentions, which are closest to Allah. Therefore, the name "Citra" can also be seen as a reminder of the presence and manifestation of Allah's mercy and kindness, and the importance of embodying them in our own actions and intentions.
